Now we use the bootstrap to estimate
the [standard error](https://morrison-lab.github.io/sds/estimation.html#def-SE) and construct a 95% [confidence interval](https://morrison-lab.github.io/sds/inference.html#def-confidence-interval).
In the non-parametric bootstrap,
each iteration applies both the model-fitting step
and the covariate standardization to the same bootstrap resample.
This joint refit-and-restandardize approach mirrors the original world in the bootstrap world
and is standard practice for this type of [estimator](https://morrison-lab.github.io/sds/estimation.html#def-estimator)
[@efron1993introduction, Chapter 6].
(An alternative would fix the covariates at the observed values,
but is less common for [g-computation](#def-g-computation) estimators.)

```{r}
#| label: bootstrap-ci
#| code-fold: show
#| cache: true
#| message: false
#| warning: false

# Set seed for reproducibility
set.seed(20260512)

# Number of bootstrap iterations in this rendered example
# (illustrative only; use >= 2000 for final CIs)
B <- 300

boot_estimates <- numeric(B)

for (b in 1:B) {

  boot_indices <- sample(
    seq_len(nrow(wcgs_clean)),
    size = nrow(wcgs_clean),
    replace = TRUE
  )

  boot_data <- wcgs_clean[boot_indices, ]

  boot_fit <- glm(
    chd69_binary ~ dibpat + age,
    data = boot_data,
    family = binomial(link = "logit")
  )

  boot_estimates[b] <- compute_marginal_rd(
    model = boot_fit,
    data = boot_data,
    exposure_var = "dibpat",
    exposed_level = "Type A",
    unexposed_level = "Type B"
  )
}

boot_se <- sd(boot_estimates)

# percentile method: quantiles of the bootstrap distribution
ci_lower <- as.numeric(quantile(boot_estimates, 0.025))
ci_upper <- as.numeric(quantile(boot_estimates, 0.975))
```

::: {#tbl-marginal-rd-results}

```{r}
#| code-fold: true

tibble(
  Estimate = marginal_rd_est,
  `Std. Error` = boot_se,
  `95% CI Lower` = ci_lower,
  `95% CI Upper` = ci_upper
) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 4)
```

[Causal marginal risk difference](#def-causal-marginal-rd) (CMRD) for Type A vs Type B behavioral pattern
(adjusted for age) via g-computation,
with [bootstrap standard error](https://morrison-lab.github.io/sds/bootstrap.html#def-bootstrap-se) and 95% confidence interval

:::
